Independent lab testing in 2025 found detectable lead in about 90 percent of the 51 toothpastes tested.

That included Davids, RiseWell, Boka, Bite, Dr. Bronner's and Tom's. Not just the mainstream tubes.

https://plasticdetox.org/articles/best-non-toxic-toothpaste-guide.html

Your supplement capsules are a microplastic source.

A 2024 study found encapsulation raised contamination in omega 3 oil by 3 to 5 times compared with the raw oil. Around 5.89 particles a day from supplements alone.

https://plasticdetox.org/articles/supplements-and-microplastics.html

A plastic cutting board sheds tens of millions of microplastic particles a year through normal chopping.

Knife grooves release polyethylene and polypropylene straight into your food. Hundreds of millions over the board's lifetime.

https://plasticdetox.org/articles/best-non-toxic-cutting-boards.html

Glyphosate is sprayed on conventional oats, wheat, lentils and chickpeas right before harvest, as a drying agent.

Pre harvest desiccation drives the highest residues in finished food, which is why organic alone is not the strongest filter here.

https://plasticdetox.org/articles/glyphosate-detox-guide.html

Bamboo toothbrush, plastic bristles.

Almost every bamboo brush on the shelf uses nylon bristles, which is the part that actually touches your mouth twice a day. The handle composts. The head does not.

https://plasticdetox.org/articles/bamboo-toothbrush-plastic-bristles.html
